facts.statement: The cost of employer-provided group term life coverage above $50,000 is taxable income to the employee.
facts.quote: the cost of $50,000 of such insurance

items.stem: An employer provides group term life insurance to employees. The cost of coverage above what amount is generally included in the employee's taxable income?
items.explanation: 26 U.S.C. § 79 includes in an employee's income the cost of employer-provided group-term life insurance only to the extent it exceeds the cost of $50,000 of coverage, less any amount the employee paid.

facts.statement: The taxable amount of group term coverage is reduced by whatever the employee paid toward it.
facts.quote: the amount (if any) paid by the employee toward the purchase of such insurance

items.stem: An employee has $150,000 of employer group term life coverage. The table cost of the excess coverage is $240 for the year, and the employee paid $60 toward the coverage through payroll deduction. How much is included in his taxable income?
items.explanation: 26 U.S.C. § 79 taxes the cost of coverage above $50,000 only to the extent it exceeds what the employee paid. $240 minus $60 is $180.

facts.statement: The cost of excess group term coverage is figured from IRS uniform premiums in 5-year age brackets, not the employer's actual premium.
facts.quote: uniform premiums (computed on the basis of 5-year age brackets)

items.stem: For federal tax purposes, the taxable cost of an employee's group term life coverage over $50,000 is measured by:
options: The employer's actual premium for that employee
IRS uniform premium rates set by 5-year age brackets
items.explanation: 26 U.S.C. § 79 measures the cost of group-term insurance using uniform premiums computed on 5-year age brackets prescribed by IRS regulations.

facts.statement: If the group term plan discriminates in favor of key employees, key employees lose the $50,000 exclusion.
facts.quote: subsection (a)(1) shall not apply with respect to any key employee

items.stem: An employer's group term life plan gives executives coverage of five times salary and rank-and-file staff a flat $10,000, and the IRS treats it as discriminatory in favor of key employees. What is the tax consequence?
options: No consequence, since $50,000 is excluded for every employee
The employer loses its deduction for the premiums
items.explanation: 26 U.S.C. § 79 denies the $50,000 exclusion to key employees under a discriminatory group-term life insurance plan.
items.retired: Key is the only option naming key employees; cue unavoidable for this rule.

facts.statement: The imputed-income rule does not apply to coverage for any period in which a charity is the sole beneficiary for the entire year.
facts.quote: a person described in section 170(c) is the sole beneficiary

items.stem: An employee has $200,000 of employer group term life coverage and names a qualified charity as sole beneficiary for the entire tax year. How much of the cost of the excess coverage is taxable to the employee?
options: The full cost of $200,000 of coverage
items.explanation: 26 U.S.C. § 79 excepts from income the cost of group-term coverage for which a qualified charity is the sole beneficiary for the entire period of the tax year.
